output.name: Ruskel — the Fid (The Lamp Road)
output.myth: When Aun cut the string, the rope came apart and the sky went up with its ends frayed. Mother Hesk sent the Gulls down to say so. Nobody could splice a rope that long from below, so Ennu the Kite-Wright carved the first Ruskel from bone, thick at the knot and fine at the point. You push the point between the strands, open a gap, lay the new strand in and draw it through. The sky ran up so fast the sailcloth nearly tore from the Reel, and Hesk caught it on the Loom Weight, Hannel, which hangs on the Lamp Road. Up in the north-west, Ruhkan the Frost-Hand is short three fingers and still ties knots, because Ruhk did not sit down about it. So at the rope-making feast the people hold up the Fid, and in autumn it rises over the Lamp Road, pointed at the cut. Aun is not there. His old tether's knot still shows if you know where to look. The Fid is always pointed at it, and never quite reaches.
output.finding: From Hannel, the Loom Weight on the Lamp Road, look a hand-span and a bit more to the east (about 23°) to find the Fid, its bone point aimed at the old knot.
